title: Origins: Broken Symmetry
description: When a field cools and must choose between equal vacua, distant regions choose differently, and where they meet, the old symmetry is trapped in a wall, a string or a knot that cannot be smoothed away. Pockets of false vacuum survive the same way. Unlocks the Topological Defect Core.

puzzle.goal: A real scalar field φ in one dimension has a potential with two equal minima, at φ = ±v, and a coupling λ: the symmetry φ → −φ is broken by whichever vacuum it falls into. Far to the left it sits at −v, far to the right at +v, and in between it must climb over the hill. Write the total energy of that static configuration: gradient energy plus potential, along the whole line.
puzzle.name: energy of a kink (domain wall) of a spontaneously broken Z₂ symmetry
puzzle.ask: The minimum-energy solution is φ = v·tanh(v x √(λ/2)), and its energy is E = (2√2/3)·√λ·v³. Find it for the coupling and vacuum value given (natural units).
puzzle.method: Energy = ∫[½φ'² + V(φ)]dx with V = (λ/4)(φ² − v²)². The minimising solution has ½φ'² = V, so dφ/dx = √(2V): change the integral to one over φ from −v to v.
